benchmarkDenominator.runner: cargo test workspace and crate-level tests
benchmarkDenominator.runnerStatus: not executed; the upstream cache is sparse/no-checkout and a Cargo run would require materializing crate source plus building Rust workspace dependencies. Full cargo test would also hydrate/build beyond the current VM cap, so this run used targeted static inventory only.
benchmarkDenominator.warning: This is stronger than the seed manifest and now includes targeted object/ref plus focused loose-ref, packed-ref, reference-store overlay, pack-index, pack-data/delta, pack generation, thin/ref-delta generation, object-database, alternates, replacements, multi-pack-index, protocol v2, fetch negotiation, fetch response/sideband, partial clone/promisor, sparse checkout/pathspec, lazy promisor hydration, push request, push response, send-pack orchestration, receive-pack stream transport, merge primitive, blob merge, recursive content-merge mapping, bounded merge-index/worktree conflict views, and directory-file conflict classification, but it is still not upstream pass parity. Next slice should add rename handling, real index/worktree writes, or concrete git-daemon/SSH/HTTP receive-pack URL adapters.

nativeImplementation.currentSlice: Native loose Git object storage, canonical commit header parsing, Git tree entry parsing/serialization, merge-base ancestry traversal, flat and recursive tree three-way merge decisions, recursive blob-content merging with conflict-marker blob output, merge-index stage views for ancestor/ours/theirs conflict entries, worktree marker-file views for content conflicts, directory-file conflict classification, loose direct/symbolic reference parsing and storage, packed-ref header/reference/peeled lookup parsing, protocol v2 capability, ls-refs parsing, fetch feature negotiation and argument building, common fetch filter specs, sparse checkout cone/non-cone path matching, lazy promisor object resolver hydration, fetch response section parsing, sideband pack/progress/error decoding, protocol v1 receive-pack push request building, generated non-delta pack handoff, REF_DELTA pack generation, thin send-pack request building, stream-backed receive-pack transport I/O, report-status parsing, receive-pack advertisement parsing, send-pack session orchestration, loose+packed reference-store overlay resolution, v2 pack-index parsing/lookup, multi-pack-index parsing/lookup, MIDX-backed object database pack selection/de-duplication, pack data entry decoding, OFS_DELTA/REF_DELTA object resolution, and pack+loose+alternate+promisor object database lookup/prefix/iteration with replacement refs.

wordpressScenario: Git-backed WordPress content workflows, package installs, Playground snapshots, and server-side repo primitives; current examples parse a WordPress deploy tree, write/read HEAD plus deployment branch refs, inspect packed branch/tag refs, parse protocol v2 ls-refs discovery responses, build a shallow blobless ref-in-want fetch request, parse protocol v2 fetch response sections and sideband pack/progress/error bytes, orchestrate a protocol v1 send-pack flow from advertised refs through generated branch/tag pack request and status response, build thin REF_DELTA send-pack payloads against remote WordPress base objects, run a receive-pack handshake/request/response cycle over native stream resources, resolve loose+packed refs, locate compacted object offsets through pack indexes and multi-pack-indexes, use MIDX-backed object database pack selection/de-duplication, read delta-resolved packed commit/blob objects, track blobless partial-clone promisor state for omitted media objects, lazily hydrate promised media objects into loose storage, apply sparse checkout materialization to a plugin-focused WordPress tree, recursively merge nested WordPress metadata/theme blobs with index stages and conflict-marker worktree output, classify nested WordPress directory-file conflicts, and traverse a pack+loose+alternate object database with replacement refs without shelling out to git.
nextTask: Add rename handling for recursive merges, real index/worktree writes, or concrete git-daemon/SSH/HTTP receive-pack URL adapters.
